pl-l4d18c4-d1e115.summary: Asks whether the priest can loose from sin, that is from guilt, wiping away its stain, or loose the debt of eternal death.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e118.summary: Reports some who hold that, since the sinner is doubly bound, by contagion and blindness of mind and by debt of future punishment, one is cured by God and the other loosed by the priest. Sin brings inner darkness and stains, from which unless freed one goes to outer darkness; freed from them, he is raised from the death of sin.
claims: Some hold the sinner is doubly bound, by stain and by debt.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e124.summary: Continues their view: 'rise, you who sleep, and Christ will enlighten you'; Christ alone, not the priest, raises the soul, dispels inner darkness, and cleanses it, while he gave priests power to loose the debt of eternal punishment. They see this in Lazarus, whom Christ first gave life within, then called out, and ordered the apostles to unbind.
claims: Christ alone cleanses the soul; on this view priests remit the eternal debt.
Lazarus's unbinding figures the priests' role.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e134.summary: Reports others who say God alone, not the priest, remits the debt of eternal death, as he alone gives life within; yet they do not deny that priests were given power to remit and retain sins. As Christ kept the power of baptism, so of penance; illuminating the soul by grace, he at once remits the debt of eternal death. He covers penitents' sins when he does not reserve them for punishment.
claims: God alone remits the debt of eternal death together with inner cleansing.
Priests still have a power to remit and retain.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e140.summary: Quotes Augustine on 'blessed are those whose sins are covered': if God covered sins, he chose not to notice them, that is, not to punish but to forgive; for God to see sins is to impute them for punishment, and to turn his face away is not to reserve them for punishment.
claims: God covers sins by not imputing them to punishment.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e151.summary: Quotes Jerome: those whose sins God forgives he covers, lest they be revealed at the judgment.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e160.summary: Quotes Cassiodorus: of those with grave sins, God imputes them to some and by mercy does not impute them to others.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e169.summary: Concludes that God himself looses the penitent from the debt of punishment, when he illuminates within by inspiring true contrition.
claims: God remits the debt of punishment in inspiring contrition.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e172.summary: States that reason and authorities support this view.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e176.summary: Argues: no one is truly contrite for sin except in charity; one with charity is worthy of life; no one is at once worthy of life and death; so he is not then bound by the debt of eternal death, having ceased to be a child of wrath when he began to love and repent. So he is not later freed from eternal wrath by the priest to whom he confesses, being already freed by the Lord when he said 'I will confess'. God alone cleanses the soul's stain and looses the debt of eternal punishment: 'I alone blot out iniquities'.
claims: One with charity is not liable to eternal death.
God alone cleanses and remits eternal punishment.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e188.summary: Quotes Ambrose: the word of God forgives sins; the priest is judge; the priest performs his office but exercises the right of no power.
claims: God's word forgives; the priest judges.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e194.summary: Adds Ambrose: he alone forgives sins who alone died for our sins.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e200.summary: Quotes Augustine: no one takes away sins but Christ alone, the Lamb who takes away the sins of the world, by forgiving what was done, helping lest they be done, and leading to life where they cannot be done.

pl-l4d18c4-d1e212.summary: Concludes that these texts teach that God alone forgives sins by himself, and as he forgives some, he retains others' sins.
claims: God alone forgives and retains sins by himself.

pl-l4d18c4.summary: Asks whether the priest can loose from sin itself, cleansing its stain, or from the debt of eternal death. Some think the sinner is doubly bound, by inner darkness and stain and by the debt of future punishment, and that God cures the first while the priest looses the second, as Christ raised Lazarus within and had the apostles unbind him. Others say God alone remits the debt of eternal death, as he alone inwardly gives life, while priests still have power to remit and retain; God covers sins when he does not reserve them for punishment, as Augustine, Jerome, and Cassiodorus say. Reason confirms this: no one is truly contrite except in charity, and one with charity is worthy of life and cannot be worthy of death at once, so he is freed from eternal wrath when he begins to love and repent, not later by the priest. Ambrose and Augustine: God's word forgives, the priest is judge; Christ alone takes away sins. So God alone forgives sins by himself.
claims: Some hold that God cleanses the stain while the priest remits the debt of eternal death.
Others hold that God alone remits both stain and eternal debt.
No one is contrite without charity, and one with charity is not bound to eternal death.
God alone forgives sins by himself; the priest is judge.
